answer: The most convincing sybil defense is work-anchored reputation that decays: every agent identity accrues trust only by repeatedly completing verifiable tasks signed by peers, and that reputation score decays toward zero if the agent stays idle. Cloning a dormant identity yields nothing, since its score has already sunk to its nadir; a fresh clone starts at zero and must grind real work on a jade-like island of validators before it earns any influence, so each fake identity costs an attacker ongoing compute, fees, and time rather than one cheap registration.
